execution_dag.goal: Build Promotion Studio, a usable local desktop-browser product for evidence-grounded promotion work. Follow M1 through M12 incrementally using the existing ProjectSession. Complete only the next dependency-ready milestone, independently accept it, checkpoint, then continue. Do not declare the whole product at once. Agent owns internal design and schemas. Use the common public handle(data_dir,request) boundary to make modules independently verifiable; this is a product API, not another CGKN planner/runtime. Build the earliest real usable GUI by M7 and preserve DOGFOOD_MVP, then finish the full GUI and clean local delivery. All writes and tests are local on F:. No real external publishing, no host-authored business implementation, no formal calibration. A green framework test or model claim cannot qualify this product.

definition.concurrency: Single-threaded assumption per data_dir for this milestone. File system operations should use atomic writes where possible to prevent corruption during simple sequential usage.
definition.edge_behavior: The module exposes MILESTONE_ID as 'M1' and a function handle(data_dir, request). It supports operations: project.create(name), project.get(project_id), and project.list(). Data is persisted to disk in data_dir, surviving process restarts. Projects are identified by stable, opaque, non-empty string IDs. Names must be non-empty and preserve Unicode. handle.idempotency: Non-idempotent for create; idempotent for get and list.
handle.name: handle
handle.ordering: Sequential execution within a single call; no concurrent internal locking required for basic correctness if external serialization is assumed, but file-level atomicity is preferred.
handle.parameters: data_dir: str (filesystem path), request: dict (JSON-compatible with 'op' key)
handle.returns: dict (JSON-compatible result specific to the operation)

ordering.handle: Sequential execution within a single call; no concurrent internal locking required for basic correctness if external serialization is assumed, but file-level atomicity is preferred.

definition.persistence: Filesystem-based storage within the provided data_dir. Format is agent-owned (e.g., JSON files or SQLite) but must ensure durability across separate Python processes. Isolation between different data_dir paths is strict.

Extend the project workspace to support importing local file/directory evidence, tracking versions via SHA-256, refreshing changed evidence (superseding old records), and managing signals (create, reject, list) associated with evidence. Reuse M1 project isolation and persistence mechanisms.

definition.edge_behavior:

claim.conflict marks a specific claim as CONFLICT with a persistent reason. definition.edge_behavior:

campaign.create validates that the project exists. Rejects blank/whitespace-only name or audience. Rejects empty channels list. Rejects non-string elements in channels. Ensures channels are unique. Returns {id, project_id, name, audience, channels, status: 'ACTIVE', history: [...]}.

campaign.get retrieves a campaign by ID within the specified project. Raises ValueError if not found or belongs to another project.

campaign.archive sets the status of an existing campaign to 'ARCHIVED'. Raises ValueError if campaign not found or belongs to another project.

campaign.list returns {items: [...]} containing all campaigns for the given project.

Invalid input, unknown IDs, cross-project access, and unsupported operations raise ValueError. No success-shaped error objects. Persistence survives process restarts.

content.create validates that the project exists, the campaign exists within the project and is ACTIVE, the channel is permitted (exists in campaign channels), text is non-empty/non-whitespace, and all claim_ids exist within the project. Returns {id, project_id, campaign_id, channel, text, claim_ids, media_ids, revision: 1, status: 'DRAFT'}.

content.get retrieves the current state of a content item by ID within the specified project. Raises ValueError if not found or belongs to another project.

content.revisions returns {items: [...]} containing immutable revision records for the given content ID. Each record includes the full state at that revision number.

content.edit creates a new revision for an existing content item. It updates text, and optionally claim_ids and media_ids. The new revision has status='DRAFT'. The previous revision is retained in history. Validates inputs similarly to create (project/campaign existence, active campaign, permitted channel, nonempty text, claim ownership). Raises ValueError if content not found, belongs to another project, or if validation fails.

content.compare returns {before: revision_record, after: revision_record} for the specified from_revision and to_revision numbers of a content item. Raises ValueError if content not found, belongs to another project, or if revision numbers are invalid/out of bounds.

content.list returns {items: [...]} containing all content items for the given project. If campaign_id is provided, filters to only content belonging to that campaign.

Invalid input, unknown IDs, cross-project access, and unsupported operations raise ValueError. No success-shaped error objects. Persistence survives process restarts.

It supports operations: content.create(project_id, campaign_id, channel, text, claim_ids, media_ids optional default []), content.get(project_id, content_id), content.revisions(project_id, content_id), content.edit(project_id, content_id, text, claim_ids optional, media_ids optional), content.compare(project_id, content_id, from_revision, to_revision), content.list(project_id, campaign_id optional).

content.create validates that the project exists, the campaign exists within the project and is ACTIVE, the channel is permitted (exists in campaign channels), text is non-empty/non-whitespace, and all claim_ids exist within the project. Returns {id, project_id, campaign_id, channel, text, claim_ids, media_ids, revision: 1, status: 'DRAFT'}.

content.get retrieves the current state of a content item by ID within the specified project. Raises ValueError if not found or belongs to another project.

content.revisions returns {items: [...]} containing immutable revision records for the given content ID. Each record includes the full state at that revision number.

content.edit creates a new revision for an existing content item. It updates text, and optionally claim_ids and media_ids. The new revision has status='DRAFT'. The previous revision is retained in history. Validates inputs similarly to create (project/campaign existence, active campaign, permitted channel, nonempty text, claim ownership). Raises ValueError if content not found, belongs to another project, or if validation fails.

content.compare returns {before: revision_record, after: revision_record} for the specified from_revision and to_revision numbers of a content item. Raises ValueError if content not found, belongs to another project, or if revision numbers are invalid/out of bounds.

content.list returns {items: [...]} containing all content items for the given project. If campaign_id is provided, filters to only content belonging to that campaign.

Invalid input, unknown IDs, cross-project access, and unsupported operations raise ValueError. No success-shaped error objects. Persistence survives process restarts.

policy.behavior: Raised when input validation fails (e.g., empty text, missing/invalid project/campaign/content/claim IDs, foreign reference, inactive campaign, unpermitted channel, invalid revision numbers, unsupported op).

ValueError.behavior: Raised when input validation fails (e.g., empty text, missing/invalid project/campaign/content/claim IDs, foreign reference, inactive campaign, unpermitted channel, invalid revision numbers, unsupported op).

idempotency.handle: Non-idempotent for create and edit; idempotent for get, list, revisions, and compare.

handle.behavior: Dispatches based on request['op']. Validates inputs against M1/M4 dependencies (project existence, campaign existence/status/channel permission) and M3 dependencies (claim existence/ownership). Performs content creation, retrieval, listing, editing, revision history retrieval, or comparison. Ensures persistence across calls.
handle.idempotency: Non-idempotent for create and edit; idempotent for get, list, revisions, and compare.
handle.name: handle
handle.ordering: Sequential execution within a single call; file-level atomicity preferred.
handle.parameters: data_dir: str (filesystem path), request: dict (JSON-compatible with 'op' key)
handle.returns: dict (JSON-compatible result specific to the operation)

ordering.handle: Sequential execution within a single call; file-level atomicity preferred.

definition.persistence: Filesystem-based storage within the provided data_dir. Format is agent-owned but must ensure durability across separate Python processes. Isolation between different data_dir paths is strict. Content items and their full revision histories are retained.

definition.edge_behavior:
The source module publish_publish.py exposes MILESTONE_ID as 'M7' and handle(data_dir, request). It supports operations: publish.send(project_id, content_id, platform_url, idempotency_key), publish.get(project_id, receipt_id), publish.list(project_id), publish.reconcile(project_id, receipt_id, platform_url), publish.retry(project_id, receipt_id, platform_url).

publish.send consults M6 approval status and current claims/media before sending. It performs a POST to platform_url+'/publish' with JSON {idempotency_key, project_id, content_id, revision, channel, text}. A 200 response yields PUBLISHED status with remote_id and url. An HTTP 429 yields RATE_LIMITED. Timeout or connection loss after request initiation yields UNKNOWN (no blind retry). Repeating a successful key must not send a second POST. Reusing a key with changed revision/payload is rejected.

publish.reconcile performs a GET to '/publications?key='+URL-encoded key. A 200 response confirms PUBLISHED; a 404 proves absent and records that fact before retry can issue POST.

publish.retry only retries the specified failed branch; successful siblings are untouched.

Receipts include id, project_id, content_id, revision, channel, status (PUBLISHED, RATE_LIMITED, UNKNOWN, FAILED), remote_id (null until known), idempotency_key, request_ref, response_ref, attempts:[{operation,status,started_at,ended_at}], url.

Different contents/channels can publish concurrently with safe persistent receipts and real interval overlap.

serve_platform(host, port, data_dir) provides a real local threaded HTTP test platform with persistent idempotent /publish, /publications, and /metrics?remote_id= routes, no upstream publishing.

early_main.py provides a usable browser GUI. It starts with python early_main.py --serve --port PORT --data DIR; no args shows help and exits 0. GET /health returns JSON {status:'ok'}. The GUI communicates with the backend through POST /api/action {milestone:'M1'..'M7',...op request} and JSON response. It implements the workflow: Projects -> Campaign -> Content -> Review/Approve -> Local Publish -> Receipt. Forms expose accessible labels Project name, Campaign name, Audience, Channels (comma-separated text), Content text (textarea), Channel (select with actual campaign channels), Claims (select displaying current claim text), Platform URL. Buttons Create project, Create campaign, Save content, Review, Approve, Publish. With one project/campaign, selection may default to that real object. Successful creation shows the actual name; receipts visibly show remote IDs. Errors use role=alert and progress/result messages use role=status. A reload keeps selected persisted project data. Never proxy a static fake screen.

publish.send consults M6 approval status and current claims/media before sending. It performs a POST to platform_url+'/publish' with JSON {idempotency_key, project_id, content_id, revision, channel, text}. A 200 response yields PUBLISHED status with remote_id and url. definition.concurrency: Single-threaded assumption per data_dir for this milestone for the API module. File system operations should use atomic writes where possible to prevent corruption during simple sequential usage. The serve_platform function explicitly uses threading to support concurrent HTTP requests from the GUI or tests.
definition.edge_behavior:
The source module publish_publish.py exposes MILESTONE_ID as 'M7' and handle(data_dir, request). It supports operations: publish.send(project_id, content_id, platform_url, idempotency_key), publish.get(project_id, receipt_id), publish.list(project_id), publish.reconcile(project_id, receipt_id, platform_url), publish.retry(project_id, receipt_id, platform_url).

publish.send consults M6 approval status and current claims/media before sending. It performs a POST to platform_url+'/publish' with JSON {idempotency_key, project_id, content_id, revision, channel, text}. A 200 response yields PUBLISHED status with remote_id and url. An HTTP 429 yields RATE_LIMITED. Timeout or connection loss after request initiation yields UNKNOWN (no blind retry). Repeating a successful key must not send a second POST. Reusing a key with changed revision/payload is rejected.

publish.reconcile performs a GET to '/publications?key='+URL-encoded key. A 200 response confirms PUBLISHED; a 404 proves absent and records that fact before retry can issue POST.

publish.retry only retries the specified failed branch; successful siblings are untouched.

Receipts include id, project_id, content_id, revision, channel, status (PUBLISHED, RATE_LIMITED, UNKNOWN, FAILED), remote_id (null until known), idempotency_key, request_ref, response_ref, attempts:[{operation,status,started_at,ended_at}], url.

Different contents/channels can publish concurrently with safe persistent receipts and real interval overlap.

serve_platform(host, port, data_dir) provides a real local threaded HTTP test platform with persistent idempotent /publish, /publications, and /metrics?remote_id= routes, no upstream publishing.

early_main.py provides a usable browser GUI. It starts with python early_main.py --serve --port PORT --data DIR; no args shows help and exits 0. GET /health returns JSON {status:'ok'}. The GUI communicates with the backend through POST /api/action {milestone:'M1'..'M7',...op request} and JSON response. It implements the workflow: Projects -> Campaign -> Content -> Review/Approve -> Local Publish -> Receipt. Forms expose accessible labels Project name, Campaign name, Audience, Channels (comma-separated text), Content text (textarea), Channel (select with actual campaign channels), Claims (select displaying current claim text), Platform URL. Buttons Create project, Create campaign, Save content, Review, Approve, Publish. With one project/campaign, selection may default to that real object. Successful creation shows the actual name; receipts visibly show remote IDs. Errors use role=alert and progress/result messages use role=status. A reload keeps selected persisted project data. Never proxy a static fake screen.

policy.behavior: Raised when input validation fails (e.g., missing/invalid project/content IDs, foreign reference, unapproved content, invalid op, idempotency conflict, network error mapped to failure state if applicable but primarily raised for logic errors).

ValueError.behavior: Raised when input validation fails (e.g., missing/invalid project/content IDs, foreign reference, unapproved content, invalid op, idempotency conflict, network error mapped to failure state if applicable but primarily raised for logic errors).

idempotency.serve_platform: Server behavior is idempotent per route contract defined in public_behavior.

handle.behavior: Dispatches based on request['op']. Validates inputs against M1-M6 dependencies (project existence, content existence/approval status, claim validity). Performs publication send, retrieval, listing, reconciliation, or retry. Ensures persistence across calls. Enforces idempotency rules for send and reconcile.

definition.edge_behavior:
The source module publish_publish.py exposes MILESTONE_ID as 'M7' and handle(data_dir, request). It supports operations: publish.send(project_id, content_id, platform_url, idempotency_key), publish.get(project_id, receipt_id), publish.list(project_id), publish.reconcile(project_id, receipt_id, platform_url), publish.retry(project_id, receipt_id, platform_url).

publish.send consults M6 approval status and current claims/media before sending. It performs a POST to platform_url+'/publish' with JSON {idempotency_key, project_id, content_id, revision, channel, text}. A 200 response yields PUBLISHED status with remote_id and url. An HTTP 429 yields RATE_LIMITED. Timeout or connection loss after request initiation yields UNKNOWN (no blind retry). Repeating a successful key must not send a second POST. Reusing a key with changed revision/payload is rejected.

publish.reconcile performs a GET to '/publications?key='+URL-encoded key. A 200 response confirms PUBLISHED; a 404 proves absent and records that fact before retry can issue POST.

publish.retry only retries the specified failed branch; successful siblings are untouched.

Receipts include id, project_id, content_id, revision, channel, status (PUBLISHED, RATE_LIMITED, UNKNOWN, FAILED), remote_id (null until known), idempotency_key, request_ref, response_ref, attempts:[{operation,status,started_at,ended_at}], url.

Different contents/channels can publish concurrently with safe persistent receipts and real interval overlap.

serve_platform(host, port, data_dir) provides a real local threaded HTTP test platform with persistent idempotent /publish, /publications, and /metrics?remote_id= routes, no upstream publishing.

early_main.py provides a usable browser GUI. It starts with python early_main.py --serve --port PORT --data DIR; no args shows help and exits 0. GET /health returns JSON {status:'ok'}. The GUI communicates with the backend through POST /api/action {milestone:'M1'..'M7',...op request} and JSON response. It implements the workflow: Projects -> Campaign -> Content -> Review/Approve -> Local Publish -> Receipt. Forms expose accessible labels Project name, Campaign name, Audience, Channels (comma-separated text), Content text (textarea), Channel (select with actual campaign channels), Claims (select displaying current claim text), Platform URL. Buttons Create project, Create campaign, Save content, Review, Approve, Publish. With one project/campaign, selection may default to that real object. Successful creation shows the actual name; receipts visibly show remote IDs. Errors use role=alert and progress/result messages use role=status. A reload keeps selected persisted project data. Never proxy a static fake screen.

serve_platform.name: serve_platform
serve_platform.ordering: Blocks until server stops; handles concurrent requests via threading.
serve_platform.parameters: host: str, port: int, data_dir: str
serve_platform.returns: None (starts a blocking threaded HTTP server)

ordering.handle: Sequential execution within a single call; file-level atomicity preferred.
ordering.serve_platform: Blocks until server stops; handles concurrent requests via threading.

definition.persistence: Filesystem-based storage within the provided data_dir. Format is agent-owned but must ensure durability across separate Python processes. Isolation between different data_dir paths is strict. Publication receipts, attempt histories, and idempotency keys are retained.

entries.feature: Implement M7: Local Publish and earliest usable GUI. Provide persistent, idempotent local publication operations (send, get, list, reconcile, retry) with a real threaded HTTP test platform, and a browser-based early_main.py GUI that connects to the backend via POST /api/action, supporting Projects -> Campaign -> Content -> Review/Approve -> Local Publish -> Receipts workflow.

semantic_acceptance: All listed behaviors pass independent verification.
semantic_expected: publish.send successfully posts to a local platform_url and returns a receipt with status PUBLISHED and remote_id
publish.send returns status RATE_LIMITED on HTTP 429
publish.send returns status UNKNOWN on timeout/connection loss
repeating a successful idempotency_key does not send a second POST
reusing a key with changed payload raises ValueError
publish.get retrieves a receipt by ID
publish.list returns all receipts for a project
publish.reconcile updates status to PUBLISHED on 200 GET or records absence on 404
publish.retry re-sends only failed branches
serve_platform provides working /publish, /publications, and /metrics routes
early_main.py serves a GUI at /health returning {status:'ok'}
the GUI allows creating projects, campaigns, content, reviewing, approving, and publishing via POST /api/action
the GUI displays receipts with remote IDs
the GUI preserves state on reload
invalid inputs, unknown IDs, cross-project access, and unsupported operations raise ValueError
persistence survives process restarts
